title: The Price of Destiny
next_chapter_hook: Just as Chen Ji was about to give up, an extremely faint Will fluctuation emerged from the depths of the Tianji Record itself—not Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul, but some older, more fundamental existence, guiding him toward a detail no one had ever noticed.

text.content: The characters on the fragment still glowed faintly with warmth, as if just awakened from ancient slumber. Chen Ji stared at the words 'Third Path', his fingertips trembling involuntarily—this was the first time since obtaining the Tianji Record that he felt fate was not merely black or white. The night wind outside howled, ruffling his robes, yet could not disperse the thickening mist in his heart.

dialogue.content: The Third Path? Hmph, do you think it's some wild flower by the roadside, to be picked whenever you please?

text.content: Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul materialized gradually from the first page, its form more ethereal than before, as if it might dissipate into the night at any moment. His turbid eyes fixed intently on the fragment in Chen Ji's hand, his lips curling into an ambiguous smile: 'Boy, do you know why no prophet throughout the ages has chosen that path?' Chen Ji's hand veins bulged as he gripped the fragment, yet forced himself to remain calm: 'I would gladly hear the details.'

Mo Xiansheng drifted above the fragment, his phantom casting mottled shadows under the moonlight: 'Because that path has never been walked to its end—not that it's impossible, but no one has ever reached the conclusion.' His voice was low and hoarse, 'Becoming the Key means burning yourself away, turning into the fuel that maintains Heaven's operation; becoming the New Heavenly Dao means severing all emotions,驾驭天地万物 with pure will. And the Third Path...' He suddenly paused, an eerie smile flickering in his eyes.

Chen Ji's heart sank sharply. He was all too familiar with Mo Xiansheng's way of speaking in half-truths—whenever he thought he was about to grasp the truth, this remnant soul guardian would slip away like a slippery loach through his fingers. 'And what about the Third Path?' His voice was extremely low, carrying a hint of danger, 'Since you brought it up, you couldn't possibly be merely teasing Chen, could you?'

Mo Xiansheng's phantom suddenly convulsed violently, as if torn by some invisible force. He clutched his chest, gasping in agony: 'E-Every time I mention it... it attracts attention... I can't...' Chen Ji's pupils contracted—he had never seen Mo Xiansheng so discomposed. This existence that had guarded the Tianji Record as a remnant soul for countless years actually feared mentioning the Third Path? What kind of being could make even a remnant soul tremble at a piece of text or a single mention?

dialogue.content: Fine, fine, this 'dare not speak' is quite something. Then let me rephrase—can you at least explain the price of becoming the Key recorded on the fourth page?

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath and redirected his gaze to the fragment. Beyond the records of the 'Third Path', the content on the fourth page made his pupils constrict sharply—it was not text, but a painting. In the painting, a human silhouette was burning, flames spreading from limbs to torso, eventually devouring the entire being. And at the flame's center, a illusory point of light was slowly dissipating, as if erased bit by bit by some force. 'Burn oneself away, becoming the sole bridge between this shore and the other.' Chen Ji read the caption beneath the image word by word, his voice exceptionally clear in the silent night. The burning flames seemed to sear his eyes through the paper—it was no ordinary fire, but the 'Void Flame' that burned existence itself.

'Not death.' Mo Xiansheng's voice sounded behind him, carrying an indescribable desolation. 'Death at least leaves ashes, leaves traces. Becoming the Key means completely disappearing from all existence in the world—no one will remember you, no place will retain you, you won't even enter reincarnation. Because your existence itself has been burned away, becoming nourishment for maintaining heaven and earth's operation.' A layer of cold sweat broke out on Chen Ji's back. He thought of his missing sister Chen Nian—if he became the Key, would his sister also forget him completely? 'Is this why none of the past prophets wanted to become the Key?' Chen Ji's voice was somewhat hoarse, 'Rather than burn away existence, they'd rather take a gamble for the position of Heavenly Dao?'

dialogue.content: Take a gamble? Do you think those who chose the path of Heavenly Dao actually gained anything?

text.content: Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul let out a low laugh, yet filled with bitterness: 'Becoming Heavenly Dao, though appearing lofty and eternal, is merely jumping from one cage into another. You will lose all emotions, all desires, everything that makes you 'human'. You will become a puppet of Heavenly Dao, day after day repeating the duty of maintaining heaven and earth's operation, until heaven and earth end.' Chen Ji fell silent. He recalled the records of the Heavenly Dao's Eye—that ultimate consciousness without concrete form. If becoming Heavenly Dao was like this, then had the Heavenly Dao's Eye once been a living person? A pitiful creature who, after making a wrong choice, could never turn back? The night wind suddenly picked up, rattling the window frames. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul wavered in the wind, his voice increasingly ethereal: 'So you understand now, boy? Both these paths, no matter which one, are dead ends. The Key will burn itself away, the Heavenly Dao will lose itself. And the Third Path...' He paused again, his phantom convulsing violently. 'What exactly is that path?' Chen Ji pressed. He knew what Mo Xiansheng feared—the 'attention' that could terrify even a remnant soul. But he still wanted to know, even if just a little clue.

choice.prompt: How does Chen Ji decide to continue pursuing information about the Third Path?

choices.description: Temporarily abandon the inquiry, pretend to accept the fate of the two paths, secretly search for other clues.
choices.visible_reward: Avoid attracting the attention of the 'Watcher'

text.content: Chen Ji slowly set down the fragment, a relieved smile appearing on his face: 'As you say, Master, Chen is enlightened.' His tone was terrifyingly calm, as if he had truly accepted this despairing answer. Mo Xiansheng was slightly startled, seemingly not expecting him to give up so easily. But only Chen Ji himself knew that a true hunter never shows his fangs to his prey.

'However...' Chen Ji suddenly shifted his direction, his gaze falling on an extremely inconspicuous symbol in the corner of the fragment, 'Has Master noticed that the edge of this page seems somewhat unusual?' Mo Xiansheng frowned: 'It's merely traces of age erosion, what's there to...' His words stopped abruptly, because Chen Ji had already brought the fragment close to the candle flame. Under the firelight's illumination, what appeared to be an ordinary symbol actually faintly gleamed—a special luster that only appeared when using the abilities of the Tianji Record.

choices.description: Directly expose Mo Xiansheng's concerns, showing willingness to bear any consequences.
choices.visible_reward: Gain more information about the Third Path
choices.risk_hint: Will directly provoke the existence that 'gazes'

text.content:
'Sir, there's no need to hide.' Chen Ji's voice suddenly turned ice-cold. 'Since Chen has come this far, life and death have long been cast aside. If that 'gaze' wishes to come, then let it come. Chen would like to see exactly what being is so forbidden that it cannot even be mentioned.' The moment his words fell, the characters on the fragmented page trembled violently, Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul twisting in agony. A scorching sensation filled the air—that was the precursor of the remnant soul about to dissipate.

'You... you brat...' Mo Xiansheng's voice came in fragments. 'Fine... fine indeed, casting aside life and death... Do you know what happened to the last person who asked such questions?'

Chen Ji's pupils contracted slightly: 'What happened?' Mo Xiansheng gave a bitter smile: 'He went mad. Completely mad. Now he's still imprisoned in the Forbidden Land of the Heavenly Eye, repeating the same question day and night—'What is the third path.' Chen Ji's back seeped with cold sweat. He suddenly realized that the distance between himself and that madman might only be a single thought away.

choices.description: Mention his missing sister Chen Nian, using family affection as a breakthrough, to request Mo Xiansheng reveal more information.
choices.visible_reward: Mo Xiansheng might reveal part of the truth due to compassion
choices.risk_hint: Will let Mo Xiansheng know Chen Nian's importance to Chen Ji

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, his voice softening several degrees: 'Sir, Chen has a younger sister... missing for many years, her whereabouts still unknown.' It was the first time he mentioned Chen Nian's existence before Mo Xiansheng. 'If Chen becomes the key or Heavenly Dao, will she forget Chen Ji completely?' Mo Xiansheng's form stiffened slightly, the trembling of his phantom diminishing by a fraction. 'You brat...' His tone was complex and hard to discern. 'So there are people you cannot let go of either.'

After a long silence, Mo Xiansheng finally sighed: 'Enough, enough. Do you know about Tianqing?' Chen Ji's heart trembled—Tianqing was precisely that fellow disciple who had sacrificed himself to block the fatal blow for him. 'Tianqing back then... had also come infinitely close to the third path.' Mo Xiansheng's voice was low. 'He discovered a flaw in the key mechanism, but ultimately failed at the last moment. Before his death, he told me the location of that flaw—it lies at the boundary between the fourth and fifth pages.' Chen Ji flipped open the fragment page and carefully searched for that so-called 'boundary' under the candlelight. Indeed, at the seam where the two pages met, there was a minute crack nearly invisible to the naked eye—one that could not be detected without specific lighting. 'So this is...' Chen Ji's voice trembled slightly. 'The clue to the third path?'

Mo Xiansheng nodded, his remnant soul becoming increasingly ethereal: 'Tianqing's sacrifice was not without meaning. He used his own existence to fill a gap in the key mechanism, transforming the third path from 'impossible' to 'possible'—though only by the slimmest margin.' Chen Ji stared at that minute crack, his heart churning with indescribable emotions. Tianqing... that always quiet, taciturn fellow disciple, that figure who had blocked the fatal blow for him at the crucial moment, had even been paving the way for him before his death? His eyes grew slightly hot, but Chen Ji forcibly suppressed this emotion. Now was not the time for grief. That thread of possibility Tianqing had bought for him, he must grasp firmly. 'That flaw... what exactly is it?' Chen Ji pressed. Just as Mo Xiansheng was about to speak, the fragment page suddenly erupted with blinding golden light, completely engulfing his voice. At the same time, Chen Ji felt an invisible force watching him—that gaze was cold, majestic, as if from the nine heavens. 'It's here.' Mo Xiansheng's voice came from within the golden light, trembling with despair. 'Boy, quickly... quickly close the fragment page...!'

Chen Ji had no time to think, instinctively closing the fragment page. The golden light vanished abruptly, and that gaze's power disappeared as well, as if it had never existed. But Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul had faded to near transparency, on the verge of dissipating entirely. 'Sir!' Chen Ji cried out, reaching out to support that illusory figure, only to grasp at emptiness. 'I'm... fine...' Mo Xiansheng's voice was extremely weak. 'Just... consumed some... rest will heal...' His phantom slowly sank into the first page, speaking the last words before disappearing: 'Boy... remember... the key to the third path... lies not in traversing it... but in making the 'path' itself... acknowledge you...' With the words finished, the remnant soul completely vanished into the Tianji Record, leaving only Chen Ji alone, staring blankly at the silent fragment page in his hands.

choices.memory_label: 天青曾发现第三条路的线索，并在临死前将位置告知墨先生

text.content: Night wind seeped through the window cracks, causing the candlelight to flicker unsteadily. Chen Ji sat alone at the table, the fragment page spread flat before him, his fingertips gently stroking that minute crack at the 'boundary'. Tianqing's voice seemed to still echo in his ears—that always低着头、quiet, taciturn fellow disciple, had actually harbored such shocking secrets. 'Make the 'path' itself acknowledge you...' Chen Ji murmured, repeating Mo Xiansheng's final words, his brow furrowed tightly. What did this mean? The path was not a person—how could it develop subjective emotions like 'acknowledgment'? Unless... unless that path itself was some kind of existence with will.

Chen Ji closed his eyes and attempted to use the Tianji Record's ability to perceive the fragment page. However, every precognitive attempt only revealed blurry, unclear images—as if some force was blocking his investigation. This feeling was very familiar to him; whenever Chen Nian appeared in his visions, the images would become blurry. But Chen Nian was not present now, yet this sense of blurriness still existed... 'Could it be...' Chen Ji's eyes snapped open, a startling thought emerging in his mind. 'The reason the third path has never been traversed is not because it's too dangerous, but because—it was never meant for humans to walk?'

Chen Ji took a deep breath, his fingertip pressing against that minute crack. He did not use the Tianji Record's ability, merely relying on instinct to feel the information contained within that crack. At first, he sensed nothing, only the rough texture of paper. But as time passed, an extremely faint warmth emanated from the crack—not the burning heat of flame, but like the body temperature of some living creature. Someone... no, something was dormant within that crack. Its presence was so faint it was nearly imperceptible, yet entirely different from the Tianji Record's own aura. If the Tianji Record was cold, rational, belonging to the existence of 'Heavenly Dao,' then the aura within that crack was warm, irrational, belonging to 'Human Dao.' 'So that's how it is...' A meaningful smile crept across Chen Ji's face.

'Not a path for humans—because this path was originally meant for the 'Dao' itself to walk. What we need to do is not become the key or Heavenly Dao, but rather... its guide.'

dialogue.content: Tianqing, you indeed left a masterful move. Unfortunately, you didn't live to witness all this... But it doesn't matter, I will walk this path to its end for you.

text.content:
Chen Ji carefully placed the fragment page into his breast, preparing to rise when he suddenly felt an unusual vibration from his怀中. It wasn't the fragment page—it was the Tianji Record's main body. He hastily took out that ancient tome, only to see the originally dim patterns on the cover slowly glowing, emanating a gentle and ancient aura. 'This is...' Chen Ji's pupils contracted. The Tianji Record, ever since he had obtained it, had remained cold and silent; even Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul could not fully control it. But now, this legendary supreme treasure was gently nuzzling against his fingers like a docile cat, as if expressing some kind of... fondness?

At that moment, an extremely faint consciousness波动传来 from the depths of the main body—that was not Mo Xiansheng, but an even more ancient, more fundamental existence. Chen Ji recognized this sensation; in the depths of the Forbidden Grounds, he had briefly touched upon such an existence. 'So you've finally noticed that crack.' An ancient and majestic voice rang in his mind. 'Throughout the ages, all prophets have been intimidated by the gaze of the 'Heavenly Eye,' only daring to wander between the two existing paths. Only you are the first to cast your gaze upon the crack.'

Chen Ji forcibly suppressed the shock in his heart, asking in a deep voice: 'Who are you? The Tianji Record's artifact spirit? Or... an existence of even higher order?' The voice fell silent for a moment, as if contemplating how to answer: 'What I am, even I myself do not know. I only know that when the first prophet obtained the Tianji Record, I already existed. I have witnessed the rise and fall of countless geniuses, seen too many people despair and wail before the two dead ends. Only you...' The voice even carried a rare note of commendation. 'You are the first to show me 'possibility.'' Chen Ji did not speak, waiting quietly for what came next. The voice continued: 'That crack was carved out by Tianqing with his life—he discovered a fatal flaw in Heavenly Dao's operation and used his own existence as the price, temporarily sealing that flaw. No one has ever walked this path, but that doesn't mean it cannot be traversed. What is needed is not power, not wisdom, but...'

choice.prompt: The voice said 'What is needed is not power, not wisdom, but...' How should Chen Ji respond?

choices.description: Without any preparation, directly demand the other party clarify what is needed.
choices.visible_cost: May come across as too eager
choices.visible_reward: The fastest way to obtain an answer
choices.risk_hint: The other party may consequently withhold information

text.content: 'But what?' Chen Ji's voice was crisp and decisive, without the slightest hesitation. The voice seemed stunned for a moment, then let out a low laugh: 'Good, good, a straightforward and decisive young man indeed. Since you don't want to beat around the bush, this old man won't hide anything either—what is needed is nothing other than 'bonds.'' Chen Ji furrowed his brow: 'Bonds?' The voice explained: 'Becoming the key or Heavenly Dao, in essence, is a process of severing all connections with the world. But the third path is precisely the opposite—it requires you to establish sufficiently deep bonds with this world, so that when you set foot on that path, the 'Dao' itself will, because it cannot bear to see you leave, actively open the gate.'

Chen Ji fell silent. This answer was both unexpected and logical. Su Qingyao, Ye Qing, Mo Xiansheng, even Tianqing... weren't these connections exactly what he had been carefully cultivating while genuinely cherishing? But the question was, were these bonds strong enough? Su Qingyao was still investigating him, Ye Qing was merely an exchange of interests, Mo Xiansheng was constantly hiding the truth... "I understand." Chen Ji nodded, "So whether the third path can be traversed depends on how deep my connection with this world is." The voice approved: "A quick learner. But you must also be careful—bonds are both keys and shackles. Once you embark on that path, everything you cherish will be exposed under the gaze of the 'Eye of Heavenly Way.' It will use every means to sever your bonds, forcing you back onto the two dead ends." A cold light flickered in Chen Ji's eyes: "Then let it try."

The voice fell silent for a long while before letting out a sigh: "You, lad, are somewhat similar to Tianqing of old... no, even more audacious than him." Chen Ji was about to speak when he felt an overwhelming exhaustion wash over him. The voice said one final time: "Remember, the existence sleeping within the crack is both the third path itself and Tianqing's final遗志. To awaken it, you need to do two things—first, find a token that proves your 'qualification'; second, prepare to pay the price. What the price is, I cannot tell you now, because even I don't know." The words faded, the consciousness fluctuation completely dissipated, and the cover of the Tianji Record returned to its usual dullness. But Chen Ji knew he had touched upon a core secret of this world. "Token... price..." he murmured, his gaze gradually deepening. Outside the window, the eastern sky was already turning bright. A new day was coming, and he had drawn one step closer to the truth of the third path.

flags_set: 获得第三条路核心信息

choices.description: Pretend to have already understood, letting the other party voluntarily reveal more information.
choices.visible_cost: May miss the best timing to ask follow-up questions
choices.visible_reward: May elicit more hidden information from the other party
choices.risk_hint: The other party may see through your intentions and refuse to speak

text.content: Chen Ji did not immediately press for more, but nodded thoughtfully: "I understand." The voice was clearly taken aback: "You... understand?" Chen Ji smiled faintly: "There's no need for前辈 to be surprised. The crack Tianqing left behind, the Tianji Record's recognition, the failures of past prophets—these pieces of information are already enough for this junior to deduce the core of the third path." He paused, then shifted gears: "However, this junior dares to guess that 前辈 appearing at this particular moment must be for more than just testing this junior's comprehension, correct?" The voice fell silent for a moment, then burst into hearty laughter: "Good lad! This old one has lived for countless years, yet this is the first time meeting a young person bold enough to play psychological tactics against this old one!" The laughter faded, and the voice became solemn: "You're right. This old one appeared because the time has come—the 'loophole' Tianqing left behind can only sustain itself for three more years. After three years, if no one takes over, the crack will completely seal shut, and the third path will vanish forever."

Chen Ji's heart tightened: "Three years?" The voice deepened: "Exactly. Within three years, you must find the token Tianqing left behind, unravel the secret it contains, and gain the recognition of the existence within the crack. These three things, not one can be omitted." Chen Ji frowned: "What is Tianqing's token?" The voice replied: "When Tianqing fell in those days, he sealed a wisp of his soul into an object. That object is now hidden in... the deepest part of the Tianqing Sect's Forbidden Grounds." Chen Ji's pupils contracted—Tianqing Sect's Forbidden Grounds, a place even Inner Sect elders could not set foot in. "This junior understands." He took a deep breath, "What else?" The voice said one final thing: "There's one more thing you must beware of—the old Sect Master Ling Yuan has already sensed the existence of Tianqing's relics. If you cannot get to the token first within three years, those relics will fall into his hands. At that time... the consequences would be unimaginable." The words faded, the consciousness fluctuation completely dissipated.

Chen Ji sat alone at the table, morning light streaming through the window onto his face. His eyes held no fear, only cold determination. Three years, that would be enough.

choices.description: Proactively reveal clues you already know, showing sincerity in exchange for more cooperation from the other party.
choices.visible_reward: May gain the other party's complete trust and more help
choices.risk_hint: The other party may use this information against you

text.content: Chen Ji deliberated for a moment, then suddenly spoke: "Since 前辈 has appeared, this junior assumes you already know all the secrets I carry. Since that's the case, this junior won't hide anything—I have a younger sister, taken by the Holy Sect as a 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key.'" The voice visibly fluctuated: "Heavenly Fate Lock Key... so that's why. No wonder there's always a blurred area in your foresight." Chen Ji nodded: "Her existence interferes with the Tianji Record's foresight. But it's also my greatest weakness." The voice fell silent for a long while before finally sighing: "Do you know, lad? This old one shouldn't be telling you these things, but your frankness has changed my mind." Chen Ji's heart surged—he had gambled correctly. The other party was not some irrational existence, but a 'will' with its own considerations. To deal with an existence at this level, honesty was反而 the best strategy.

The voice continued: "Your sister Chen Nian, her being taken was no coincidence. The Heavenly Fate Lock Key is another 'loophole' in the Heavenly Way's operation—the fools at the Holy Sect think they can control this power, but they don't realize they are the ones being used as pieces." A cold light flashed in Chen Ji's eyes: "前辈's meaning is... Chen Nian's existence is also some kind of 'opportunity'?" The voice approved: "A quick learner. The Heavenly Fate Lock Key and the third path are two sides of the same coin. One is responsible for 'locking' the gap in fate, the other for 'opening' the path forward. If you can find your sister within three years and merge the two threads into one... at that time, this old one will give you a tremendous surprise." The words fell, the consciousness fluctuation grew increasingly faint: "Remember, lad. The Eye of Heavenly Way will not sit idle watching you grow. From now on, every choice you make, every action you take, will be watched by it. But as long as you are careful enough, decisive enough... the third path may not just be a dead end after all."

The cover of the Tianji Record completely dimmed, yet Chen Ji could not calm himself for a long time. He looked down at the ancient scroll in his hands, muttering to himself: "Chen Nian... three more years..." Outside the window, daylight had fully broken. A new day, a new game of chess, and his opponents had expanded from the three major sects and the Demonic Holy Sect to that ultimate existence called the "Eye of Heavenly Way."

choices.memory_label: 天命锁钥与第三条路是一枚硬币的两面

text.content: The morning light gradually became glaring, yet Chen Ji remained motionless where he sat. In his mind, all the fragments of information were rapidly processing—the third path, Tianqing's遗志, Ling Yuan's threat, Chen Nian's whereabouts, the three-year deadline... these clues that seemed completely unrelated were gradually weaving into a complete web within his deduction. "The key burns itself, the Heavenly Way loses itself, the third path..." he murmured, "What is needed is bonds, is having the 'Way' itself recognize me." The corner of his lips lifted slightly, revealing a meaningful smile: "Interesting."

Chen Ji placed the Tianji Record's main body back into his embrace, his fingertips unconsciously stroking the subtle crack on the残页. Tianqing's aura seemed to still linger there, faint yet stubborn, as if silently conveying something. Three years, neither long nor short. There was too much he needed to accomplish within these three years—enhancing strength, consolidating position, gathering intelligence, recruiting allies, guarding against Ling Yuan, finding Chen Nian... and now, one more thing: finding the relics hidden in the depths of the Tianqing Sect's Forbidden Grounds. "Ling Yuan..." A cold glint flashed in Chen Ji's eyes. That old fox who outwardly sheltered him while secretly harboring ill intentions had probably already sensed something. The Tianqing Sect's Forbidden Grounds was the first obstacle he must breach. But before that, he needed to make much more preparation.

Just then, a light knock came at the door. "Brother Chen?" It was Su Qingyao's voice, cold yet carrying a thread of concern, "You stayed up all night, are you alright?" Chen Ji stood up, stretching his stiff body. He stored the残页 and Tianji Record's main body into a hidden compartment, ensuring nothing could be discovered, before going to open the door. Outside, Su Qingyao in her cyan garments stood in the morning light. A faint worry lingered between her brows, but upon seeing Chen Ji safe and sound, that worry was quickly replaced by her usual coldness. "Nothing's wrong, just studying some problems with cultivation techniques." Chen Ji displayed a warm, harmless smile, "Thank you for worrying, Sister Su." Su Qingyao stared at him for a moment, seemingly trying to find some flaw on his face, but ultimately gave up. "Good that you're fine." She turned to leave, then suddenly stopped, "By the way, today at noon, there will be an assembly in the Inner Sect regarding forbidden grounds security. The elders seem to be discussing strengthening the forbidden grounds' defenses... if you're interested, you may come to observe." Saying this, she left without looking back.

Chen Ji closed the door, his smile gradually deepening. A forbidden grounds security assembly? It seemed Ling Yuan had already begun acting—this was precisely an excellent opportunity to learn about the forbidden grounds' layout. Su Qingyao... this woman who had been investigating him had unknowingly become his best source of intelligence. Chen Ji gazed at her departing figure, a complex emotion flickering in his eyes. This woman was too sharp, too persistent. He needed to think of a way to completely dispel her pursuit—or turn her from a dangerous investigator into a reliable guardian. "Shared fate buff..." he murmured, "Perhaps it's time to speed up the progress." Outside the window, the sun had fully risen. A new day, a new challenge, and Chen Ji had made full preparations.
